units.title: Component 01: Studies and applications in psychology 1

outcomes.text: Name types of crime: violent, drug related, acquisitive, sexual and anti-social.
Explain criminal behaviour as a social construct shaped by norms and culture.
Explain how crime is measured by official statistics and self-report.
Explain identification with role models, observation and imitation in criminality.
Explain vicarious and direct reinforcement and internalisation.
Evaluate the theory, including the nature/nurture debate.
Describe and evaluate Cooper and Mackie (1986) on video games and aggression in children.
Explain extraversion, neuroticism and psychoticism in relation to criminal behaviour.
Link the central nervous system and arousal levels to the criminal personality.
Explain synapses, dopaminergic neurons and an overactive dopamine system in psychoticism.
Explain the roles of dopamine reward, reticular activating system and cerebral cortex in extraversion.
Explain the autonomic nervous system and limbic system in neuroticism.
Explain early socialisation and conditioning difficulties, and evaluate the theory including individual differences.
Describe and evaluate Heaven (1996) on delinquency, extraversion, psychoticism and self-esteem.
Evaluate rehabilitation, including restorative justice and positive role models, in reducing anti-social behaviour.
Evaluate punishment and deterrents: prisons, community sentences and fines.
Describe the stages of development: pre-natal, childhood, adolescence and adulthood.
Describe brain development: structures, nervous system, neurons and synapses.
Explain IQ tests as a measure of intelligence.
Describe the four stages: sensori-motor, pre-operational, concrete-operational and formal operational.
Explain assimilation and accommodation.
Explain object permanence, animism and egocentrism.
Explain decentration, reversibility and conservation, and evaluate the theory including reductionism/holism.
Describe and evaluate Piaget (1952) on conservation of number.
Explain Dweck's fixed and growth mindsets and praise for effort.
Explain Willingham's myth of learning styles and the importance of meaning for learning.
Evaluate learning theories, including the nature/nurture debate.
Describe and evaluate Blackwell et al. (2007) on mindsets.
Apply Piaget to education: key stages, readiness, active learning and intelligence.
Apply learning theories to education through growth mindsets and teaching for meaning.
Define mental health, including the mental health continuum.
Describe current prevalence of mental health problems by age, gender and sexual orientation.
Explain changes over time in classification and attitudes since the 1959 Mental Health Act.
Explain effects of stigma and discrimination before and after diagnosis.
Explain effects of mental health problems on wider society, including care in the community.
Describe the clinical characteristics of schizophrenia as set out in the ICD.
Give key statistics: prevalence, age, sex, ethnicity and recovery rates.
Explain the dopamine hypothesis, including dopaminergic neurons and synaptic transmission.
Explain brain dysfunction in schizophrenia: volume, activity and the frontal lobes, hippocampus and temporal lobes.
Evaluate the biological theory including nature/nurture.
Explain the social drift theory and evaluate it, including cause and effect.
Describe and evaluate Daniel, Weinberger, Jones et al. (1991) on amphetamine and cerebral blood flow.
Describe the clinical characteristics of depression as set out in the ICD.
Give key statistics: prevalence, age, sex, ethnicity and recovery rates.
Explain the social rank theory, including the evolutionary function and lower rank reducing conflict.
Evaluate the social rank theory including reductionism/holism.
Explain the ABC model: rational and irrational beliefs, activating events, beliefs and consequences.
Evaluate the ABC model including free will/determinism.
Describe and evaluate Tandoc et al. (2015) on Facebook use, envy and depression.
Explain how anti-psychotics and anti-depressants treat schizophrenia and depression via neurons and synapses.
Explain how psychotherapy treats schizophrenia and depression.
Describe neuropsychology in studying these conditions, including neuropsychological tests and brain imaging.

units.title: Component 02: Studies and applications in psychology 2

outcomes.text: Define conformity, including majority influence.
Define collective and crowd behaviour, pro-social and anti-social.
Define obedience to authority figures.
Explain majority influence on conformity and deindividuation in crowds.
Explain culture's effect on pro-social and anti-social behaviour and authority figures' effect on obedience.
Evaluate situational explanations including free will/determinism.
Describe and evaluate Bickman (1974) on obedience and the power of a uniform.
Explain self-esteem and conformity, locus of control in crowds, morality and pro/anti-social behaviour.
Explain the authoritarian personality and obedience.
Explain brain influences: hippocampal volume in self-esteem and prefrontal cortex in morality.
Evaluate dispositional explanations, including generalisability.
Describe and evaluate NatCen (2011) on the August riots in Tottenham.
Apply minority influence to changing attitudes and reducing mental health stigma and discrimination.
Apply majority influence to changing attitudes and reducing mental health stigma and discrimination.
Describe information processing stages: input, encoding, storage, retrieval and output.
Explain forgetting by decay, displacement and retrieval failure.
Explain brain and memory: hippocampus in anterograde amnesia, frontal lobe in retrograde amnesia, cerebellum in procedural memory.
Describe the sensory store, short-term memory and long-term memory.
Compare stores by duration, capacity and encoding.
Evaluate the model, including rehearsal versus meaning.
Describe and evaluate Wilson, Kopelman and Kapur (2008) on Clive Wearing.
Explain schemas and the roles of experience and expectation.
Explain confabulation, distortion and leading questions.
Evaluate the theory including reductionism/holism.
Describe and evaluate Braun, Ellis and Loftus (2002) on advertising and memory.
Explain how advertisers use cues, repetition, avoiding overload and autobiographical advertising to aid recall.
Describe neuropsychology for measuring memory, including the Wechsler Memory Scale.
Describe functions and benefits of sleep: healthy brain, physical repair and emotional stability.
Describe the stages of the sleep cycle and when dreaming occurs.
Explain the pineal gland and melatonin.
Explain sleep onset and sleep maintenance insomnia.
Explain endogenous pacemakers and exogenous zeitgebers in sleep.
Explain the unconscious mind, repression and wish fulfilment.
Distinguish manifest from latent dream content and evaluate the theory, including subjectivity.
Describe and evaluate Freud (1918) on the Wolfman.
Explain the role of REM sleep and the limbic system during sleep.
Explain neuron activity in the pons and synthesis in the cerebral cortex.
Evaluate the theory including reductionism/holism.
Describe and evaluate Williams et al. (1992) on bizarreness in dreams.
Explain insomnia features, the nervous system and relaxation techniques.
Explain the physical environment and sleep hygiene in treating insomnia.
Explain the impact of hypothalamus damage on sleep.
State null and alternative hypotheses.
Write hypotheses predicting differences, correlations or no pattern.
Explain independent, dependent and co-variables and how each is manipulated or measured.
Explain extraneous variables and how to control them, including standardisation.
Compare repeated measures and independent measures designs.
Explain target populations, sample size, representativeness and generalisability.
Compare random, opportunity and self-selected sampling.
Apply the principles of sampling to scientific data.
Explain ethical issues: informed consent, psychological harm and deception.
Explain debriefing, right to withdraw and confidentiality.
Describe the British Psychological Society's Code of Ethics and Conduct.
Compare laboratory, field and natural experiments with their strengths and weaknesses.
Compare structured and unstructured interviews.
Compare open questions, closed questions and rating scales.
Compare naturalistic, controlled, overt, covert, participant and non-participant observation.
Explain case studies, qualitative data and small samples.
Explain correlations and positive, negative and zero relationships.
Compare quantitative, qualitative, primary and secondary data and their strengths.
Calculate mode (including modal class), median and mean.
Calculate range, ratios, percentages and fractions.
Use decimal and standard form, decimal places and significant figures.
Interpret normal distributions and make estimations from data.
Draw and read frequency tables, bar charts, pie charts, histograms, line graphs and scatter diagrams.
Explain internal, external and inter-rater reliability.
Explain ecological, population and construct validity.
Explain demand characteristics, observer effect and social desirability.
Identify gender, cultural, age, experimenter, observer and questioning bias.
